title: How Chronos-Architecture Handles a fork When the Parent Has Gigabytes of Memory: Runtime Invariants and Algorithmic Bounds in Python

abstract: Operating systems employ copy-on-write (COW) mechanisms to optimize process forking, deferring physical memory duplication until a write operation occurs. This work presents a Python-based simulation of a COW memory architecture, modeling page allocation, reference counting, and state transitions during fork and write events. We formalize the invariant that the sum of reference counts across all processes equals the total allocated pages, ensuring memory consistency. We analyze the asymptotic complexity of page lookup and COW triggering, demonstrating $O(1)$ average-case performance for dictionary-based page registries. Empirical benchmarks on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor yield a mean latency of 60265.08 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 16,593 ops/s. The results validate the structural integrity of the COW mechanism under synthetic load, providing a reproducible baseline for evaluating memory management algorithms in managed runtimes. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261026_070139_how_aether-framework_handles_a}
